stem.text: A car moves along a straight road with positive velocity v(t) meters per second, where v is differentiable and t is measured in seconds. Measured values are v(0) = 4, v(2) = 12, v(3) = 16, v(7) = 8. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{7} v(t)\,dt \), the distance, in meters, that the car travels from t = 0 to t = 7, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 2 \cdot \frac{4 + 12}{2} = 16 \); \( 1 \cdot \frac{12 + 16}{2} = 14 \); \( 4 \cdot \frac{16 + 8}{2} = 48 \).

distractor_derivations.A: trapezoidal sum with the common width (b - a)/3 used for every subinterval
distractor_derivations.B: left Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.C: trapezoid area taken as width times the sum of the two endpoint values, with no division by 2
